sentence: Genotypes A/A + A/G of rs6311 are associated with increased severity of high-risk behaviors (self-injury, suicidality, harm to others) when treated with escitalopram in people with familial risk for bipolar I disorder and clinically significant depression and/or anxiety symptoms as compared to genotype G/G.
explanation: In escitalopram-treated adolescents (12–17 years) at familial risk for bipolar I disorder, carriers of the −1438A allele (A/A or A/G) showed greater increases on the TEASAP high-risk behaviors subscale than G/G; the study reports this as a novel finding in a small sample without providing p-values in the excerpt.
citations: We recruited outpatient youth aged 12–17 years who had at least one first-degree relative with bipolar I disorder and clinically significant depression and/or anxiety symptoms (operationalized as a Children's Depression Rating Scale-Revised (Poznanski et al., [1984](#B41)) score >35 or a Pediatric Anxiety Rating Scale (Anonymous, [2002](#B5)) score ≥15.
Thus, only the escitalopram-treated youth were included.

Participants with *HTR2A A/A* or *A/G* genotypes had a greater increase in TEASAP “Self-injury, Suicidality, and Harm to Others” subscale scores relative to those with *HTR2A G/G* genotypes (*p* = 0.017).

*HTR2A* genotype comparisons were made between homozygotes for the −1438G>A (rs6311) allele (*G/G*) and homozygotes and carriers for −1438A (*A/A*, *A/G*), based on the results of prior studies of associations between *HTR2A* and antidepressant-related adverse events (Kato et al., [2006](#B29); Murphy et al., [2003](#B35); Wilkie et al., [2009](#B57)).

Because the CPIC categories used for analysis are metabolizer phenotypes (e.g., participants with normal rates of CYP2C19 metabolism), and not discrete genotypes (e.g., participants with *CYP2C19 *1/*1* alleles), CYP metabolizer groups are referred to throughout this study as phenotypic (rather than genotypic) groups.
CYP2C19 phenotype influences escitalopram pharmacokinetics whereas CYP2D6 phenotype does not.
